text:
jordan: Heads up — discovered a partial service-account JSON (private_key_id and client_email) in partner-ingest GCS audit logs. Looks like logs were shipped before redaction. Not sure if ciphertext was stored or plaintext. Can we triage and start containment?

lina: Ugh. Can you paste an example line (redacted) and the GCS path? We need to know blast radius (which project, which objects). :eyes:

jordan: gs://redwood-partner-logs/2026-03-22/ingest-12345.log — snippet: `{"actor":..., "protoPayload": {"request": {"body": "... \"client_email\": \"service-account@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com\", \"private_key_id\": \"abcd1234...\" ..."}}}`. I masked the long key.

ben: @jordan good catch. First step: stop any downstream replay of that bucket. ben-ops: can you pause log forwarding to SIEM and any partner pipelines?

alex: paused forwarding for that prefix (confirmed). Also added a temp storage ACL to limit reads to ops/security for now.

priya: If private_key is present in logs, treat it as compromised. Plan: rotate the SA key, revoke any tokens issued with it, and ensure KMS-wrapped backups are safe. Who owns rotation for that SA?

lina: @priya agree. We should also check Vault rewrite hooks — maybe a bad consumer dumped the JSON somewhere. I'll search vault audit logs for wrap/unwrap and who requested secrets for that SA.

jordan: Quick grep I ran: ```grep -n "service-account@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com" /mnt/partner-logs/* | head``` returned multiple files across 3 dates. Looks like an ingestion bug sanitized only later in pipeline.

sec-bot: automated-alert: KMS Audit stream shows UNWRAP operations from runner-ci in project-team-a at 2026-03-22T18:12Z. See internal ticket #SEC-3921.

ben: Good signal from sec-bot. Lina: can you map UNWRAP operations to Vault/VPC egress? We need to know if plaintext left our infra.

lina: On it. Early finding: unwraps came from a CI runner service account in build-project-a, but the KMS caller identity is a trusted, ephemeral SA. Need to validate whether plaintext output was logged by our ingestion service or by partner ELK.

alex: Two quick mitigation ops I recommend now: 1) Rotate the compromised SA keys (generate new key, revoke old). 2) Force rekey/evict any long-lived tokens associated with the SA. I'm pushing a small runbook: `./runbooks/sa-rotate.sh service-account@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

priya: Also add a Vault policy/role review — any service that had access to decrypt/wrap should be scoped down until we confirm no misuse. I'll open a PR to tighten the role and tag it for rollback after verification.

jordan: Compliance question — retention of logs: partner contract requires 90d retention. We need to ensure we don't delete partner copies without legal ok. For our side, can we redact and rotate locally then notify partner?

lina: Yes, don't delete partner data until legal signs off. We can redact our copies, snapshot the raw data for forensics (secure bucket, limited ACL), rotate keys, and then coordinate an ask to partner to scrub on their end.

sec-bot: checklist update: created incident channel #sec-3921, flagged high severity, and generated an artifacts key for forensics: forensic-1776543210.

ben: Ownership: lina leads triage + KMS audit mapping. alex handles immediate ops (pause forward, ACLs, rotate SA). priya owns Vault RBAC changes and PRs. jordan coordinates partner notif and legal handoff. I'll own the runbook execution.

priya: Quick note on Vault + KMS integrations — if any wrapped ciphertext was stored in partner logs (instead of plaintext), we still want to rotate the KMS key if the key policy allowed cross-project unwraps. I'll run a KMS key policy audit and post results here.

alex: Rotation timeline: SA key rotated within 30m, tokens revoked in 1h, Vault role change PR by EOD, KMS policy audit results by tomorrow.

jordan: For transparency: SR blackbox scan to find any other exposed keys: `jq -r 'paths | select(.[] | tostring | test("private_key_id|client_email"))' *.json` — share findings here when done.

lina: Found two other service emails referenced; opening a coordinated rotation plan for them as precaution.

ben: After rotations, we should run an auth re-issue for CI runners and update CI secrets store. Also check image caches for embedded creds.

priya: I'll add short-lived KMS wrapping for any new keys and enable CMEK audit logs forwarding to SIEM with higher fidelity. Also propose a policy: no raw SA JSON allowed in logs — add a scrubber in ingest pipeline.

jordan: Action items summary (from thread so far): pause forwarding (alex), ACL snapshot (alex), SA rotate + revoke (alex), KMS policy audit (priya), Vault RBAC tighten PR (priya), KMS unwrap mapping / forensics (lina), partner + legal notif (jordan), runbox scans and CI secret rotate (ben).

lina: Will post update in 30m with KMS unwrap mapping and whether plaintext left our infra.

alex: Rotation done for compromised SA, old key revoked — changed CI secrets and restarted affected pipelines. Will paste commands in incident channel.

sec-bot: automated-update: ticket SEC-3921 status -> containment: true, evidence_bucket: gs://forensic-1776543210, next_step: legal_review.

jordan: Thanks all. Once legal clears partner message, I'll ping partner security and ask for deletion or redaction of their copies. Keep me posted on Vault RBAC PR and KMS audit results.

priya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/vault/pulls/987 — tightens role to `wrap-only` for build runners. Tagging @lina for review.

lina: Reviewed and approved. Merging now.

ben: Follow-up todo: schedule a short postmortem + add a unit test in ingestion pipeline asserting no SA JSON tokens pass through.

jordan: Agreed. I'll schedule the postmortem for tomorrow 10am PT. Thank you team. :thumbsup:
